Bug_Title: Beans in "@Configuration" class should have different names
Bug_Details:
Naming conventions play a crucial role in maintaining code clarity and readability. The uniqueness of bean names in Spring configurations is vital
to the clarity and readability of the code. When two beans share the same name within a configuration, it is not obvious to the reader which bean is
being referred to. This leads to potential misunderstandings and errors.
Bug_Explanation: In the above code, there are two beans in the @Configuration class, 'a' and 'anotherA'. 'a' and 'anotherA' share the same name. This can lead to confusion and errors.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the `showBug` method of the `Config` class. This method returns the bean named 'anotherA', which has the same name as another bean in the configuration class. This creates confusion and can potentially cause errors.
